$comment: THE THROAT. ONE VOICE, and it is the one the room needs: somebody who has been coming into this mountain for thirty years and is completely unbothered by it. The Ascent must not turn the Aurelians back into a mystery -- that story finished at the Temple -- so the lampwright treats the cut stone as what it is to her, which is old work by good people, and nobody says the word Aurelian anywhere on this mountain.

lines: Thirty-one years I have carried oil up that flight for lamps that were never going to take oil.
They were never out. They were waiting. There is a difference and I am going to sit down.
There is a stair at the back with lamps down both walls and no way to light them.
No wick, no oil hole, no nothing. Just a cup of stone with a mark in it.
I bring oil up anyway. Thirty-one years. My husband thinks I am ridiculous.
